rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes '256' to '255' in the COMMENT '// Use 256 threads per block for better occupancy' on line 44. The actual executable code 'const int block_size = 256;' remains unchanged. Comments are stripped during compilation, so both versions compile to identical CUDA kernels.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation is a true equivalent mutant because it only modifies text within a C++ comment string. Comments have no semantic meaning in C++/CUDA and are discarded by the compiler during preprocessing. The actual block_size constant used in the kernel launch configuration remains 256 in both the original and mutated code. Since the compiled CUDA kernels are bitwise identical (same block_size=256, same vec_size=4, same grid_size calculation), no input values can ever produce different outputs between the original and mutant. The Layer 2 dynamic testing confirmed bitwise identical outputs across 112 test rounds, and this is expected behavior for a comment-only mutation.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under any testing strategy because the mutation only affects a comment, which has no effect on program execution. The actual code (block_size = 256) is unchanged between original and mutant. Both versions compile to identical machine code.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should exclude comments from mutation targets, as comment mutations always produce equivalent mutants. This wastes testing resources and pollutes mutation score metrics. Consider adding a pre-filter to skip mutations where the target token appears within comment delimiters (// ... or /* ... */).
